import mir_eval
import numpy as np

# Ensure chromagram has 12 rows and matches the length of times
N = times.shape[0]
chromagram = np.ones((12, N)) * 0.5

# Ensure non-negative magnitudes for proper sonification
chromagram_positive = np.maximum(0, chromagram)

fs = 8000
max_time = np.max(times) if N > 0 else 1.0
expected_length = int(np.ceil(max_time * fs)) + fs

# Perform reverse synthesis of the chromagram
signal = mir_eval.sonify.chroma(
    chromagram_positive, 
    times, 
    fs, 
    length=expected_length
)

# Verify the output is a 1D numpy array of the requested length
assert isinstance(signal, np.ndarray), "Output must be a numpy array"
assert signal.ndim == 1, "Output must be a 1D array"
assert len(signal) == expected_length, f"Expected length {expected_length}, got {len(signal)}"

print(f"__CHECK__ chroma {len(signal)}")
